name: А
cursiveLookalike: Resembles handwritten Latin 'A' and 'a'
a1Note: Always pronounced like 'ah' when stressed.
b1Note: Undergoes weak reduction to [ɐ] in immediately pre-tonic syllables.
c1Note: Retains open central unrounded quality strictly under primary tonic stress.

name: Бэ
cursiveLookalike: Lowercase cursive looks like Latin 'd' or a digit 6 with a top arm.
a1Note: Voiced 'b' sound like in English.
b1Note: Devoices to [p] at the end of words or before voiceless consonants.
c1Note: Undergoes regressive voice assimilation, triggering voicing in preceding obstruents.

name: Вэ
soundHint: v as in voice (NOT English B, even though it looks like it!
cursiveLookalike: Looks identical to English 'B'/'b' but sounds like 'V'
a1Note: False friend: written like Latin 'B', but sounds like English 'V'.
b1Note: Devoices to [f] in word-final position (e.g. гото́в -> ga-TOF).
c1Note: Voiced labiodental fricative (a type of consonant sound produced by placing the top teeth against the bottom lip and forcing air through the narrow gap to create friction or a hissing sound), it acts transparently in certain cluster voicing rules.

name: Гэ
cursiveLookalike: lowercase cursive looks like a backward 's' or Latin 'r' hook (г)
a1Note: Hard 'g' sound as in 'get'.
b1Note: Pronounced as [v] in genitive adjective andings -ого / -его (e.g. его -> ye-VO).
c1Note: Devoices to [k], except in religious words where it spirantizes to [x] (Бог -> [box]).

name: Дэ
cursiveLookalike: Lowercase cursive looks exactly like Latin handwritten 'g'
a1Note: Dental 'd' sound made with the tongue touching upper teeth.
b1Note: Devoices to [t] word-finally and palatalizes before soft vowels.
c1Note: Subject to alveolar dental assimilation and total elision in clusters like -здн-.

name: E
cursiveLookalike: Resembles handwritten Latin 'E'/'e'
a1Note: Sounds like 'ye' at the start of words or after vowels.
b1Note: Reduces to a short [ɪ] (ikanye) in unstressed syllables.
c1Note: Softens the preceding consonant and loses its initial [j] glide.

name: Ё
cursiveLookalike: Cursive 'e' shape written with two distinctive dots on top
a1Note: Always carries tonic stress in native Russian words.
b1Note: Softens the preceding consonant while rendering an open-mid [o] vowel.
c1Note: Historically developed from stressed /e/ preceding non-palatalized consonants.

name: Жэ
soundHint: zh as in measure or beige
cursiveLookalike: Written with intersecting central loops resembling a beetle
a1Note: Deep, buzzy 'zh' sound; always grammatically hard.
b1Note: Devoices to hard [ʂ] (like 'sh') word-finally or before unvoiced consonants.
c1Note: Voiced retroflex sibilant; subsequent vowels are pronounced hard regardless of spelling.

name: Зэ
cursiveLookalike: Looks like the digit '3' with a descending tail loop in lowercase
a1Note: Pronounced like English 'z'
b1Note: Devoices to [s] at the end of words (e.g. глаз -> glas).
c1Note: Assimilates completely in place of articulation before sibilants (сшить -> [ʂːɨtʲ]).

name: И
cursiveLookalike: Lowercase cursive looks identical to English handwritten 'u'
a1Note: Clean 'ee' sound; softens preceding consonants.
b1Note: Pronounced as hard [ɨ] when following always-hard consonants (ж, ш, ц).
c1Note: High front tense unrounded vowel; triggers secondary palatalization.

name: Й кра́ткое
cursiveLookalike: Cursive 'u' shape with a curved breve diacritic over the top
a1Note: Semi-vowel glide; almost always follows another vowel in diphthongs.
b1Note: Never forms its own syllable; combines into diphthongs like ой, ей, ай.
c1Note: Voiced palatal approximant [j]; phonologically non-syllabic.

name: Ка
cursiveLookalike: Resembles handwritten Latin 'k'
a1Note: Crisp 'k' sound without heavy English aspiration.
b1Note: Voices to [ɡ] before voiced obstruents through regressive assimilation.
c1Note: Velar plosive; historically resistant to palatalization before front vowels in roots.

name: Эль
cursiveLookalike: Starts with a small introductory hook on the bottom left
a1Note: Hard 'l' is dark, pronounced with the back of the tongue raised.
b1Note: Softens drastically before soft vowels or ь to a bright European [lʲ].
c1Note: the 'L' sound is with two different styles: a regular, clear 'L' versus a deeper, 'dark L' sound

name: Эм
cursiveLookalike: Starts with a low left hook to distinguish from cursive 'т'
a1Note: Standard bilabial nasal like English 'm'.
b1Note: Remains voiced across word boundaries; does not devoice at word end.
c1Note: Pairs into distinct hard [m] and palatalized [mʲ] phonemes.

name: Эн
soundHint: n as in net (NOT English H)
cursiveLookalike: Looks identical to Latin capital 'H' and lowercase 'h'
a1Note: False friend: looks like English 'H', but pronounced like 'N'.
b1Note: Dental articulation; tongue contacts the back of the upper teeth.
c1Note: Maintains sonorant status; never participates in terminal devoicing.

name: О
cursiveLookalike: Identical to Latin handwritten 'O' / 'o'
a1Note: Sounds like 'o' only when stressed; reduces to 'ah' when unstressed.
b1Note: Subject to akanye: reduces to [ɐ] pre-tonically and [ə] in other unstressed positions.
c1Note: Mid back rounded vowel; reflects historical Common Slavic /o/.

name: Пэ
cursiveLookalike: Lowercase cursive looks exactly like Latin handwritten 'n'
a1Note: Unaspirated 'p' sound like in Spanish or French.
b1Note: Causes preceding voiced consonants to devoice via assimilation.
c1Note: Voiceless bilabial plosive; pairs systematically with voiced counterpart /b/.

name: Эр
cursiveLookalike: Looks identical to English 'P' / 'p' with a descender
a1Note: False friend: looks like English 'P', but pronounced as a rolled 'R'.
b1Note: Alveolar trill; requires tip-of-tongue vibration against the alveolar ridge.
c1Note: Sonorant liquid; retains voicing in terminal positions.

name: Эс
soundHint: s as in sun (NOT English C/k)
cursiveLookalike: Looks identical to Latin 'C' / 'c'
a1Note: False friend: looks like English 'C', but always sounds like 'S'.
b1Note: Voices to [z] before voiced consonants (e.g. сдо́ба -> ZDO-ba).
c1Note: Voiceless dental sibilant fricative.

name: Тэ
cursiveLookalike: Lowercase cursive looks exactly like English handwritten 'm'
a1Note: Dental 't' pronounced with tongue against the front upper teeth.
b1Note: Silent in complex consonant clusters like стн (че́стный -> CHES-ny).
c1Note: Palatalizes before soft vowels to an affricated dental [t͡sʲ] variant.

name: У
soundHint: oo as in boot (NOT English Y)
cursiveLookalike: Looks identical to Latin 'Y' / 'y'
a1Note: False friend: looks like English 'Y', but sounds like 'oo' in 'boot'.
b1Note: Does not undergo severe vowel reduction when unstressed.
c1Note: High back rounded vowel; causes labialization of preceding consonants.

name: Эф
cursiveLookalike: Vertical center stem flanked by two symmetrical oval loops
a1Note: Pronounced like English 'f'.
b1Note: Primarily appears in loanwords and terminal devoicings of 'в'.
c1Note: Voiceless labiodental fricative; absent in Proto-Slavic native stems.

name: Ха
soundHint: kh as in Scottish loch (NOT English X/ks)
cursiveLookalike: Looks identical to Latin 'X' / 'x'
a1Note: False friend: looks like English 'X', but sounds like a raspy 'kh'.
b1Note: Velar fricative produced by constricting airflow in the back of the mouth.
c1Note: Voiceless velar fricative [x]; does not assimilate to [ɣ] except dialectally.

name: Цэ
cursiveLookalike: Square bottom right corner terminating in a tiny descending tail
a1Note: Always hard; sounds like 'ts' blended together.
b1Note: Following 'и' is always pronounced as hard [ɨ] (цирк -> tsyrk).
c1Note: Voiceless alveolar affricate; permanently non-palatalized in modern standard Russian.

name: Че
cursiveLookalike: Resembles handwritten digit '4' or an open cup
a1Note: Always soft; sounds like a crisp 'ch'.
b1Note: Irregularly pronounced as [ʂ] ('sh') in specific words (что -> shto, коне́чно -> ka-NYESH-na).
c1Note: Voiceless postalveolar affricate; inherent palatalization [t͡ɕ].

name: Ша
cursiveLookalike: Three vertical stems; cursive writers underline it to distinguish from 'т'
a1Note: Always hard; pronounce with tongue pulled back.
b1Note: Devoices preceding consonants and hardens any subsequent vowels.
c1Note: Voiceless retroflex sibilant fricative [ʂ].

name: Ща
cursiveLookalike: Shape of 'ш' with a small descending tail at the bottom right
a1Note: Always soft and long; sounds like 'sh' pronounced with smiling lips.
b1Note: A single long soft sibilant [ɕː], not two separate hard consonants.
c1Note: Long voiceless alveolo-palatal fricative derived historically from *stj / *skj.

name: Твёрдый знак
cursiveLookalike: Looks like lowercase 'ь' with a top horizontal flag pointing left
a1Note: Silent letter; creates a sharp pause before iotated vowels.
b1Note: Prevents the preceding consonant from softening before е, ё, ю, я.
c1Note: Historical reflex of the short back yer *ъ; now functions strictly as a non-palatalizing separator.

name: Ы
soundHint: guttural 'i' (like being punched in the gut)
cursiveLookalike: A rounded loop joined directly to an upright stroke
a1Note: Tense gut sound made by pulling your tongue back while making an 'ee' sound.
b1Note: Only occurs after hard consonants; never starts a native Russian word.
c1Note: Close central unrounded vowel [ɨ]; phonemic status remains a classic debate in Russian linguistics.

name: Мягкий знак
cursiveLookalike: Resembles a lowercase Latin 'b' without the upper tall stem
a1Note: Silent letter; softens (palatalizes) the consonant right before it.
b1Note: Can act as a separator before vowels (e.g. семья́ -> seem-YAH).
c1Note: Reflex of the historical short front yer *ь; causes secondary palatal articulation.

name: Э
cursiveLookalike: Backwards 'C' with a middle horizontal dash
a1Note: Open 'eh' sound without any initial 'y' sound.
b1Note: Does not palatalize preceding consonants; common in loanwords.
c1Note: Mid front unrounded vowel [ɛ] without iotated glide.

name: Ю
cursiveLookalike: Vertical stem joined by a horizontal crossbar to an oval 'O'
a1Note: Sounds like 'yu' at start of words or after vowels.
b1Note: Softens the preceding consonant and sounds like pure 'oo'.
c1Note: Iotated vowel [ju]; triggers terminal devoicing in stems like юг -> [juk].

name: Я
cursiveLookalike: Mirrored Latin capital 'R' beginning with a smooth baseline stroke
a1Note: Sounds like 'ya' at the start of words or after vowels; means 'I'.
b1Note: Reduces to [ɪ] (ikanye) in unstressed pre-tonic syllables (язы́к -> yee-ZYK).
c1Note: Iotated vowel; reflects both historical nasal *ę and palatalized *a.
